summary: The two statistical repairs are real improvements and both survive checking. The nearest-rank arithmetic is exact — ceil(0.50×21)=11, ceil(0.95×21)=20, ceil(0.99×21)=21 — and naming the estimator removes an ambiguity I had not identified as one. The regression rule now pairs the previous and candidate binaries on the same VM in randomized order, and forces a rebaseline when image identity or CPU brand differs, which closes a confound I passed over at D-094 turn 3: the same contract permits weekly image rolls without a successor, so a same-class comparison across a roll would have measured image drift rather than code. Simulating the five edits gives eighteen named identifiers, one reserved cell which is G13, and zero survivals of either PARTLY MET or 'fixed runner image'. One note, on a preflight tolerance whose sizing depends on an external unit convention I cannot verify.

selfCorrection.summary: Codex's ADV-D094-T3-01 identifies a confound in the regression rule I reviewed and passed at D-094 turn 3, and ADV-D094-T3-02 finds a real defect in a clause I considered and explicitly declined to raise.
selfCorrection.onTheRegressionConfound: At D-094 turn 3 the contract said release-to-release regression compares distributions 'on the same fleet class, not on a reused VM and not across a successor-triggering class change'. I verified that the cross-VM rule existed and had the components the prompt named, and treated it as complete. What I did not do is read it against the neighbouring clause, which permits a weekly runner-image roll within the same OS family without a successor. Those two together mean a release-over-release comparison can span two different images while still being 'the same fleet class', so the D-006 ten-percent rule would have been applied to a difference that includes image drift. The failure is specific: confirming that a required component is present is not the same as testing whether it works under variation the same entry elsewhere allows. When one clause admits a source of variation and another defines a comparison, the two have to be read together.
selfCorrection.onTheEstimator: I did consider the sample size at D-094 turn 3 and recorded in that verdict that I was declining to raise it, on the reasoning that at N=11 the p95 and p99 collapse toward the maximum and so err strict rather than lax. That reasoning was about direction and it was not wrong, but it was answering a smaller question than the one available. The actual defect was that no estimator was named at all: 'p50/p95/p99 of N=11' does not determine a value, because linear-interpolation and nearest-rank methods disagree, and a threshold gate whose computation is undefined cannot be audited. D-098 fixes that by naming nearest-rank with rank = ceil(p × N) and stating the resulting ranks. I checked the arithmetic and it is right. Having decided a clause was safe, I stopped instead of asking whether it was well defined.
selfCorrection.pattern: This is the third finding in this family that I passed and Codex caught, after the second stale v2 clause at D-093 and the D-054 scope question at D-095. The common shape is that I test the question the prompt puts in front of me and stop at a defensible answer, rather than asking what else the clause has to be true against.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, fail-closed preflight item 4: 'RAM GiB = observed_bytes/1024³ matches table 7/14/16 within ±0.75 GiB'
notesNonBlocking.observation: The check computes the observation in GiB and compares it against the table's figures, but does not say whether those figures are decimal GB or GiB, and the answer decides whether three of four platforms can ever pass. If the table means GiB, the ±0.75 GiB window is generous slack for kernel reserve and everything passes. If it means decimal GB, the conversions are 7 GB = 6.52 GiB, 14 GB = 13.04 GiB and 16 GB = 14.90 GiB, so the deviations are 0.48, 0.96 and 1.10 GiB — the 7 row passes and the 14 and 16 rows fail permanently. The asymmetry is itself the signal: a tolerance sized for kernel-reserve slack does not scale with capacity, whereas the GB-to-GiB gap does, which suggests the window was not derived from the unit question. I raise this as a note rather than a finding for three reasons. The observable and the computation are specified precisely, so what is undetermined is an external documentation convention I cannot reach from this repository. Preflight is fail-closed and invalid jobs are 'replaced, not counted', so a mis-sized tolerance cannot corrupt a measurement — it can only prevent sampling, which surfaces on the first run rather than silently. And the entry is a specification for a harness that does not exist yet. Stating the unit explicitly, or expressing the bound as a fraction of the advertised figure, would settle it in a clause.

The attack 'ADV-D094-T3-02 not landed (N/estimator still collapses p95 and p99)' fails, and I recomputed rather than accepting the stated ranks. With N=21 and nearest-rank, ceil(0.50×21)=11, ceil(0.95×21)=20 and ceil(0.99×21)=21, exactly the ranks the entry gives. The p99 is still the maximum observation, but of twenty-one samples rather than eleven, and the estimator is now named so the value is determined rather than method-dependent. The entry also separates the `--help` and `--version` series instead of pooling them, which matters because D-006 sets its thresholds against those commands individually.

The attack 'ADV-D094-T3-01 not landed (unpaired same-class historical compare still allowed)' fails, and the fix is properly constructed rather than a disclaimer. First qualified release uses absolute numerals only. Later comparisons run the previous qualified binary and the candidate on each of the N VMs in randomized order, so the ten-percent rule applies to paired per-percentile results — pairing controls VM-to-VM variation and randomised order controls sequence effects. When image identity or CPU brand differs the entry requires a rebaseline, states that the rule 'does not span a rebaseline', and names the case explicitly: 'Weekly image rolls force rebaseline, not unpaired same-class compare.' That last sentence is the one that closes the confound.

The attack 'ADV-D094-T3-03 not landed (preflight underspecified)' fails on the substance. Preflight is nine fail-closed items with observables named for each — `sysctl -n hw.ncpu` / `nproc` for CPU count, `hw.memsize` / `MemTotal` for RAM, `df -k /` for storage — and it now requires host, executable and process architecture all to match the class rather than architecture alone. The translation check is applied to both macOS classes, not only the Intel one, which is the stronger position: an x86_64 binary running translated on the arm64 runner would otherwise have passed unexamined. Invalid jobs are 'replaced, not counted', so a failed preflight cannot dilute a distribution. My one reservation about a parameter is at D098-N-1 and does not touch the structure.

The attack 'still calls labels one machine / exact pins' fails: 'Fleet class = workflow label + documented public-repo CPU/RAM/storage/arch row. New VM per job. Labels are not one machine and not an immutable digest.'

The attack 'silent Rosetta or Apple-Silicon-hosted Intel' fails on the header, the three-way architecture match, the two-class translation check with its four branches, and the closing 'Never Intel on Apple Silicon. Never Rosetta.'

The attack 'changes D-006 numeric threshold numerals' fails, and the class-trade table records what changing the binding does to them, per platform and in both directions — stricter on macos-arm64, larger RAM on both Linux rows with 'Extra RAM is not a license to grow the process', and the first sized Intel pin. The warrant is stated separately from OBS-T3-02, which is named as the Intel reason and expressly 'not the sole warrant for the other three'. Those two elements are the D094-T2-SF-1 repair carried forward from the parked cycle, and they survive intact.

The attack 'flips condition 4 to MET without a complete fleet contract' fails, and the naming arithmetic is verified by simulation rather than by reading. Applying all five edits to a copy of the live register yields exactly eighteen 'named: harness.' strings, one surviving 'reserved, not named' cell which is G13, zero occurrences of 'PARTLY MET' anywhere, and zero survivals of 'fixed runner image' — a phrase the fleet contract would otherwise leave false.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The two statistical repairs are the substance of this cycle and both hold up when checked rather than read. Naming nearest-rank with ceil(p×N) turns 'p99 of N' from an underdetermined phrase into a computable rank, and I recomputed 11, 20 and 21 rather than trusting them. The paired regression rule is the better fix of the two: running the previous and candidate binaries on the same VM in randomized order, and forcing a rebaseline whenever image identity or CPU brand moves, means the ten-percent rule measures the binary rather than the fleet. Both of those came from Codex, and both correct clauses I passed at D-094 turn 3 — one I verified as present without testing it against the image-roll permission two paragraphs away, and one I looked at directly and set aside on reasoning that answered a smaller question than the clause deserved. I have recorded both rather than folding them into the general account. My single note is a preflight tolerance whose sizing turns on whether a published table means GB or GiB, which I cannot determine from here; it is fail-closed either way, so the worst case is blocked sampling on the first run rather than a wrong number.
